candidates.item: does not allow sending messages to the internet
candidates.why_interesting: A free public email service that explicitly blocks outbound email to the internet is a genuinely unusual technical constraint — most free email services exist precisely to send external email. This is quirky and specific to them.
candidates.recency_note: Pulled from homepage text at time of step-1 research; date unknown.

candidates.item: suggests blocking problematic users by IP rather than domain
candidates.why_interesting: Rather than accepting domain-level blocklisting (the norm for free email providers), they actively lobby receiving mail servers to target individual IPs — an unusually proactive and technically specific stance on reputation management.
candidates.recency_note: Pulled from homepage text at time of step-1 research; date unknown.

candidates.item: claims it is NOT a throwaway/disposable email service and emails won't bounce
candidates.why_interesting: Explicitly distancing from the throwaway-email category is an unusual positioning move for a free public email provider — most in this space either lean into the disposable angle or say nothing. The blunt public disclaimer is a distinctive, self-aware stance.
candidates.recency_note: Pulled from homepage text at time of step-1 research; date unknown.
